newsitem.title: USA: Columbia posts stronger fourth-quarter results.
newsitem.headline: Columbia posts stronger fourth-quarter results.

text.p: Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp., the nation's largest health care services provider, Wednesday posted strong fourth-quarter results, citing improved services and continued growth through acquisitions and joint ventures.

Profits rose to $414 million, or 61 cents a share, in the quarter ended Dec. 31, from $354 million, or 53 cents a share, in the year-ago period. Revenues rose 12 percent to a record $5.1 billion from $4.6 billion.

Columbia Chairman and CEO Richard Scott attributed the company's strong performance to a "focus on developing services that are convenient and customer-oriented, developing better outcome measurements and building customer loyalty."
Same-facility net revenues grew 10 percent in the fourth quarter, based upon adjusted admissions growth of 7 percent and inpatient admissions growth of 5 percent, it said.
Surgery cases at Nashville, Tenn.-based Columbia's hospitals and ambulatory surgery centres rose 6 percent on a same-facility basis in the fourth quarter.
On a consolidated basis, Columbia's adjusted admissions rose 11 percent, inpatient admissions rose 7 percent and surgery cases grew 10 percent for full-year 1996.

As a result of Coumbia's growth in home care services, outpatient surgery and other ancillary services, outpatient revenues made up 39 percent of total patient revenues in the fourth quarter, up from 37 percent in the 1995 period.

Columbia said it spent $2.3 billion last year to modernise and expand services at its existing health care facilities and networks, and to acquire, build or create joint ventures that added 28 additional hospitals as well as other health care entities.
On Jan. 15, Columbia announced a definitive agreement to acquire Value Health Inc., a speciality healthcare services company, for about $1.3 billion in stock.

Columbia said 57 of its hospitals were commended by the Joint Commission on Accreditation of Healthcare Organisations in the past year, making it the nation's most commended health care group, with 124 citations.
Columbia has 343 hospitals, 136 outpatient surgery centres, more than 550 home care locations and extensive ancillary services in 37 states, England and Switzerland.
Columbia's stock rose 62.5 cents to $41.75 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-morning.
